subject: Business
title: Platform Strategy: Building Ecosystems
description: Learn Platform Strategy: Building Ecosystems in one minute.

hook.text: Microsoft didn't beat competitors with better software. It won by making everyone else build on Windows.

buildup.text: A platform strategy creates value by enabling interactions between producers and consumers.

discovery.text: Platforms beat products because each new participant adds value. More apps attract more users attract more apps.

twist.text: Platform power is almost impossible to compete away once established. The ecosystem itself is the moat.

climax.text: Apple's App Store generates $80B+ annually. Apple builds the platform; millions of developers build the value.

punchline.text: Build the stage. Let others perform on it.

quiz.question: Why are platforms harder to compete against than products?
options: The ecosystem of participants creates a self-reinforcing moat
Platform companies have better marketing teams

details.summary: Platform strategy builds a business model that creates value by facilitating exchanges between two or more interdependent groups, such as buyers and sellers or developers and users. Platforms become more valuable as more participants join, creating powerful network effects.
details.whyItMatters: Platforms dominate the modern economy with seven of the ten most valuable companies being platform businesses. Understanding platform dynamics is essential for building, competing with, or participating in platform ecosystems.
takeaways: Platforms create value by connecting interdependent groups of participants
Network effects make platforms more valuable as participation grows
Solving the chicken-and-egg problem of initial adoption is the key challenge

faq.question: How do platforms solve the chicken-and-egg problem?
faq.answer: Common strategies include subsidizing one side to attract the other, starting with a single-player mode that provides standalone value, seeding supply by creating initial content or inventory, and launching in a concentrated niche before expanding. Each platform requires a tailored approach.

faq.question: What makes platform businesses difficult to compete against?
faq.answer: Network effects create increasing returns to scale. Switching costs lock in participants. Data advantages compound over time. Multi-homing costs discourage users from using multiple platforms. These dynamics create winner-take-all or winner-take-most market outcomes.
